counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.033292939945716679 to 0.005, keeping steps=22 and all bodies/G identical; finer resolution removes the close-encounter integration error

explanation: Two heavy bodies on crossing orbits undergo a deep close encounter near step 21-22 (distance 1.197 at step 20 -> 0.762 at step 21 -> 0.465 at step 22, comparable to softening 0.3). Potential deepens from -747 to -1666 and kinetic rises to ~2081 with speeds ~7.75 and ~13.86. With outer dt~0.0333 (max allowed) the adaptive substepping (24-30 substeps) is insufficient to resolve pericenter of the softened Kepler problem, so leapfrog loses ~140 energy (drift, not oscillation) while momentum stays conserved, tripping energy_conserved. Reducing only dt to 0.005 eliminates the violation.
vision_note: Two blue bodies on converging paths approach each other from steps 19 to 21. By step 22 they nearly overlap in a close encounter with sharply curving trails.
